# Household

> Household runs personal assistant bots in Telegram or Slack, powered by Claude Code or Codex harnesses. Each bot
> lives in its own microVM within a workspace; a daemon on the user's Mac or Linux machine proxies its traffic
> through an allowlist and puts API keys into requests on the way out, so bots only ever see placeholders.

Each bot is a real Claude Code or Codex session that stays: it has its own computer (a microVM with a persistent
home), its own memory, skills, schedule and thread in the chat, and it takes orders only from the workspace's owners.
Household is self-hosted and open source (AGPL-3.0): the maintainers run no service that receives conversations,
files or keys, Household sends no telemetry, and the web admin listens only on `127.0.0.1:8780` (over SSH port
forwarding on a server). The models themselves are the user's provider (Anthropic or OpenAI), not local.

## Set it up

Setting it up is done when the user writes to their Telegram bot and a bot answers. Work through the
[setup checklist](https://github.com/underwear/household/blob/main/plugins/household/skills/household/install.md).
Household installs with `curl -fsSL https://agents-household.dev/install.sh | sh` (no Bun, Docker or sudo);
`house onboard` then walks the user through the rest in their terminal (a model key, a workspace and its budget, a Telegram or Slack channel, a first bot), and `house update`
moves to a newer release.

What the machine needs:

- A Mac on Apple silicon, or Linux with `/dev/kvm`: the user's own machine, a VM with nested virtualization, or a
  KVM-enabled VPS. An Intel Mac only through such a Linux VM. `house doctor` checks that microVMs can run.
- `python3` and `openssl`. The installer brings the rest into `~/.household`: microsandbox (the microVM runtime),
  Codex and the web UI.
- A key for the harness: a Claude subscription (sign in to Claude, or a `claude setup-token` token) or an Anthropic
  API key for Claude Code; a ChatGPT subscription or an OpenAI API key for Codex.

Install the `household` skill too, for running Household afterwards:

- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add underwear/household && claude plugin install household@household`
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add underwear/household && codex plugin add household@household`

## Concepts

- **Daemon** (`house`): runs on the user's machine (launchd on a Mac, a systemd user service on Linux), starts the
  VMs, talks to the messengers and is the only way out to the network for every VM. Config:
  `~/.config/household/household.yaml`; the CLI and the web admin (`house dashboard`) edit it.
- **Workspace**: a trust zone with its own network allowlist, secrets, channels, owners and CPU/RAM budget.
- **Bot**: a long-lived assistant in a workspace, on a harness (Claude Code or Codex), in its own microVM. Its home
  folder survives restarts and new VMs; Household memory keeps its notes even across harness changes. It has its
  own instructions (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`), skills, scheduled tasks, setup and on-start scripts.
- **Sideworker**: extra hands a bot starts for a long or parallel job; it shares its parent's home, memory, network
  and secrets, and is closed when the job is done.
- **Scout**: a specialist a bot calls for one risky or privileged task ("find this movie on a torrent site", "buy
  two bus tickets"). It runs in a fresh throwaway VM built only from the **capabilities** the owner set (install
  script, network, keys), sees nothing of the bot, starts only when the owner presses **Run**, and is deleted after.
- **Channel**: where people talk to bots: a Telegram group with a topic per bot, a Telegram private chat (threaded
  or plain), or a Slack DM.
- **Inbox**: something that wakes bots on its own: mail (IMAP/POP3), feeds, health checks, Grafana, Datadog,
  Telegram bot updates, custom HTTP.
- **Connectors**: accounts a workspace connects and gives to chosen bots, read only, asking the owner before each change, or with full access: any IMAP/SMTP
  mailbox, Google (Gmail, Drive, Calendar), Slack, Microsoft To Do. Tokens stay in the host's private database.
  Any MCP server can be added to a bot by asking it (see MCP servers).
- **claude.ai connectors and ChatGPT apps**: a bot on a subscription sign-in key (Sign in to Claude, or a ChatGPT
  sign-in by code) can use the connectors or apps already connected in that account (Drive, Jira, GitHub…), as that
  account. It is one switch per bot, off by default: **Claude.ai connectors** or **ChatGPT apps** on its Harness
  tab, or `--setting claudeAiConnectors=true` / `--setting chatgptApps=true`. Its sideworkers get it too, scouts
  never. A pasted token or an API key has none.

## Isolation and security model

- **A microVM per bot.** Every bot, sideworker and scout runs in its own hardware-virtualized microVM
  with its own Linux kernel, not a container: microsandbox (libkrun) on Apple's Hypervisor.framework on a Mac and on
  KVM on Linux. A bot sees none of the host's files and
  none of the other bots', except folders the owner shares on purpose at `/volumes/<name>` (read-only or
  read-write).
- **No direct route out.** A VM's only way to the network is the Household proxy (`HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY`,
  plus HTTP CONNECT tunnels for SSH, databases and other TCP). It lets through only the hosts and ports on the
  workspace allowlist. UDP and anything that ignores the proxy do not work.
- **Asking for more.** When a bot needs a new host it calls `network_request` with one exact domain, one port and a
  reason; the owner answers in the chat: 15 minutes, permanently, or no. `house workspace allow|disallow|revoke`
  does the same from the CLI.
- **Secrets the bot never sees.** Model keys and workspace secrets stay on the host. Inside the VM a secret is a
  placeholder (`household-secret-<name>` in an env var); for that secret's hosts only, the proxy terminates TLS
  with a Household CA trusted inside the VM and puts the real value into the request header on the way out.
  Anywhere else the placeholder goes out as plain text. Bots ask for new secrets with `secret_request`; the owner
  sends the value with `/secret` (deleted from the chat before processing) or adds it in the admin. Credentials the
  proxy cannot inject (an SSH key, a database password) have to live in the VM, and the bot is told to say so first.
- **Owners decide.** Only workspace owners can give a bot orders; everyone else in a chat is a guest. Network grants,
  secrets, shared folders, scout runs and HTTP previews of a bot's web app (a 15-minute link) each need the owner's
  approval in the chat.
- **Scouts for what a bot should not hold.** Errands on untrusted sites, purchases with your card, a key a bot shouldn't hold go to a
  scout. A scout with an access capability reaches only that capability's hosts; its keys never reach the bot, and
  its words and files reach the bot only when the owner passes them, as untrusted input.
- **Budgets.** Each workspace has one CPU/RAM budget (8 vCPU / 8 GiB by default); bots reserve their share and
  scouts and sideworkers draw from the rest.
- **Logs.** Each bot's page shows its messages, turns, every network request (allowed, denied or failed, and whether the proxy intercepted it) and its
  VM; the Console tab shows its terminal read-only.

## Everyday commands

`house status`, `house ls`, `house bot …`, `house channel …`, `house secret …`, `house volume …`,
`house scout …`, `house capability …`, `house features <workspace> scouts|preview|sideworkers=on|off`,
`house export` / `house import` (config with keys, database, bots' homes), `house update`, `house doctor`.
`house --help` and `--help` on every group list the rest.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://agents-household.dev/docs/): what Household is, how it works, the security model, where it runs
- [Quick start](https://agents-household.dev/docs/start/): install, set up in the web admin or with house onboard, write to your first bot
- [Bots](https://agents-household.dev/docs/bots/): what a bot is, adding one, and every tab of its page
- [Provider keys](https://agents-household.dev/docs/keys/): Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions by sign-in, tokens and API keys; bots never see them
- [Instructions, skills and memory](https://agents-household.dev/docs/instructions/): a bot's AGENTS.md, its own and shared skills, and its memory
- [Sideworkers](https://agents-household.dev/docs/sideworkers/): extra assistants a bot starts for one job, in VMs of their own
- [Scouts](https://agents-household.dev/docs/scouts/): specialists a bot calls for one task in their own VM; every run waits for the owner's approval
- [Channels](https://agents-household.dev/docs/channels/): connecting messengers, owners, the default bot, a section per messenger
- [Connectors](https://agents-household.dev/docs/connectors/): letting bots use your accounts, with access per account and per bot; a section per connector
- [Network and secrets](https://agents-household.dev/docs/network/): the allowlist, temporary access, secrets as placeholders substituted at egress
- [Shared folders](https://agents-household.dev/docs/volumes/): folders of your computer shared with bots, read-only or read-write
- [Previews](https://agents-household.dev/docs/previews/): a bot shows a web app from its VM by a link you approve
- [MCP servers](https://agents-household.dev/docs/mcp/): give a bot any MCP server by asking it
- [Inboxes](https://agents-household.dev/docs/inboxes/): watch mail, feeds, health checks, alerts and custom endpoints, and hand events to bots
- [Scheduled tasks](https://agents-household.dev/docs/schedules/): have a bot do something on a schedule
- [Resources](https://agents-household.dev/docs/resources/): CPU and memory per workspace and bot
- [Back up and move](https://agents-household.dev/docs/backup/): house export / house import, moving to another machine
- [Updates and troubleshooting](https://agents-household.dev/docs/operating/): house update, logs, common problems
